主要内容: Kraft Heinz shares fell more than 13% on Thursday, hitting an all-time low, as the packaged food giant delayed its quarterly filing and disclosed write-downs totaling $1.22 billion. The company had previously received a subpoena from the Securities and Exchange Commission into its accounting policies and internal controls. The SEC investigation led to an internal review, causing Kraft Heinz to delay its annual report filing twice. In May, Warren Buffett, one of the company's largest investors, mentioned that Kraft Heinz was in "a dispute with its auditor." The internal review identified adjustments that resulted in an understatement of the cost of products sold totaling $208 million, including misstatements of $175 million. Kraft Heinz then cautioned that the SEC investigation was ongoing. The company also delayed filing its quarterly reports for the first and second quarters of 2019 due to a "material weakness" in its cash flow projections allocation to certain brands. Kraft Heinz experienced a significant drop in its stock price following the release of its earnings report. The company reported a decline in net income for the first half of the year, with earnings dropping to half of what they were in the same period in 2018. Additionally, Kraft Heinz recorded a $744 million write-down for its Eastern emerging markets, Brazilian, U.S. refrigerated, and Latin America exports businesses. The company also wrote down its Miracle Whip, Velveeta, Lunchables, Maxwell House, Philadelphia, and Cool Whip brands by $474 million. Despite exploring options for its Maxwell House brand, including a potential sale, the company has faced limited interest. Kraft Heinz also pulled the sale of several other brands and delayed the potential sale of its Ore-Ida frozen potato business. For the second quarter ended June 29, the company earned $449 million, or 37 cents per share, down from $754 million, or 62 cents per share, a year earlier. Excluding impairment charges, earnings were 78 cents per share, which was better than the 75 cents per share analysts had expected. Revenue fell to $6.41 billion, from $6.69 billion a year ago, and sales were below estimates of $6.58 billion. The company did not provide an outlook for this year's financial targets.
